chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh al-Nakhas from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed dhihar with his wife but found nothing to free a slave, nor anything to give in charity, nor the strength to fast. He said, 'He should fast eighteen days: for every ten poor people, three days.' As for feeding, it should be half a sa' for each poor person.

key_terms.صَاعٍ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume for dry goods)
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Dhihar (verbal divorce where the husband compares his wife to his mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for dhihar if one cannot fast, give charity, or free a slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Tahdhib, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the graduated expiation for Dhihar, prescribing a specific combination of fasting and feeding when the primary options are unaffordable. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportional ease (taysir), where the penalty is scaled to the individual's financial capacity, ensuring the obligation remains accessible to the poor.
